images.title: A torch makes a bigger shadow
images.purpose: Shows in a side view how rays from a torch spread so the shadow on the wall is twice the toy's height.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Side view with no ground line: a torch at the left, a toy upright in the middle, a wall at the right, two straight rays from the torch past the toy to the wall.
images.exact_structure: A small torch drawn as a simple dark rounded shape at the left, its bulb as an amber #E69F00 dot. An invisible horizontal axis runs from the bulb perpendicular to the wall. A toy drawn as a teal #0072B2 upright bar 10 units tall, 50 units right of the bulb, centred on that axis (5 units above it, 5 below). A wall as a vertical grey bar 100 units right of the bulb. Two thin amber rays from the bulb: one through the top of the toy, one through the bottom, each continuing to the wall. The rays meet the wall 10 units above and 10 units below the axis; the shadow is a thick dark grey segment on the wall between them, 20 units tall. Labels: 'torch' under the torch, 'toy 10 cm' beside the toy, 'shadow 20 cm' beside the shadow, '50 cm' on a thin dimension line from bulb to toy, '100 cm' on a thin dimension line below from bulb to wall.

images.takeaway: Rays spread from a nearby torch, so the shadow is larger: 10 × 100 ÷ 50 = 20 cm.
images.description: Shows in a side view how rays from a torch spread so the shadow on the wall is twice the toy's height.
images.context: Concept T12.C1; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Move the torch to 150 cm and the shadow becomes about 13.3 cm, closer to the projection.

image_decisions.why: Why a shadow grows is a ray picture; one side view with two rays shows the similar triangles.
